sections.html:
Oak Lawn has several local steps: a village transfer stamp, a point-of-sale sewer inspection for houses, and a stamp refund program for some sellers. Each step has its own form, so starting early protects the closing date.

The village borders Chicago on the southwest side. Population is 56,450 (July 2025 estimate), the median owner-occupied value is $281,200, and 82.5% of homes are owner-occupied. Most homes sit on compact lots. Mean travel time to work is 30.8 minutes. The sections below follow the order of a typical sale: the village stamp, the sewer inspection, refunds, Cook County recording and property tax.

The village tax is 5.00 per 1,000 of value, enacted January 1, 1982, with the seller liable and an exemption letter attached to the recording as proof. Exempt transfers pay no fee. The village adds that senior sellers of a primary residence are now exempt, with the rules in section 3 of its exemption list.

  • Request stamps or an exemption letter from the Finance Department. The village accepts only electronic fillable forms, and handwritten forms are rejected.
  • Questions go to 708-499-7775 or transferstamps@oaklawn-il.gov.
  • A Utility Billing Account Change form handles the water account.
  • The village's own address is 9446 S. Raymond St., phone 708.636.4400.

State and county taxes sit on top: 50 cents per $500 for the state under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and 25 cents per $500 for Cook County.

Oak Lawn requires a sewer inspection, called I&I, for single-family homes and qualifying townhomes before the transfer stamp. Schedule it well ahead of closing.

  1. Use the village's online permit portal, search the property address, choose Residential and the Transfer Stamp Sewer Inspection (I&I) permit type, and enter N/A for work details.
  2. The village reviews the request and emails either a record number with a scheduling link or a note that no inspection is needed.
  3. Pick a date for the I&I Sewer inspection. It happens between 10am and 2pm, and someone over 18 must be present with access to the interior.
  4. After the inspection, a payment link arrives by email for $100, and the results follow once payment is made.

Ask the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 whether your address needs the inspection, since the village screens each request first.

Village ordinance 3-2-7 allows a refund in three cases. Each requires the seller to have owned and lived in the house as a principal residence without renting any part of it.

Oak Lawn stamp refund cases
Refund caseWho qualifies
ReinvestmentSeller buys or builds a single-family home or condominium inside the village within one year of paying the tax, and lives there
Senior citizenOne-time refund for a seller age 65 or older who owned and occupied the home for more than one year, with a rule for co-owners under 60
Family saleSale to a child, parent, grandparent, brother, sister or grandchild, step relatives included

Refund requests are due within one year of the sale. Packets for each case are linked from the village's refund page, and the Finance Department's refund line is 708-499-7777.

sections.h2: Cook County recording and property tax
sections.html:
Oak Lawn deeds are recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St. The seller is liable for both the state and county stamps, and a PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

For assessments, look up your 14-digit PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to see your township. The south and west suburban townships follow a triennial reassessment cycle. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for installment status on the parcel, and expect the title company to prorate the year's bill at closing.

Elementary schools include Kolb, Lieb, Harnew, Columbus Manor, Covington, Hannum, Hometown, Kolmar and Sward, with Simmons and Oak Lawn-Hometown as middle schools. Oak Lawn Community High School and Harold L. Richards High School are the two public high schools. Metra's SouthWest Service runs from the Oak Lawn station toward downtown Chicago, and Advocate Christ Medical Center is one of the largest hospitals in the state.

The village maintains 22 parks on more than 300 acres, with outdoor pools, an indoor ice arena, two fitness centers, an indoor racquet center and an 18-hole golf course. The median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,000 a month, a useful point when a buyer weighs a house here against a rental.

An updated house near 95th Street or the Metra station usually does well in a listing. A house with sewer problems, an old rental history or an estate behind it often fits a direct as-is sale better, since the inspection and stamp steps still apply either way.

Whichever route you take, work in this order: confirm with Finance whether the sewer inspection applies, book it, pay the $100 fee, request the stamp or exemption letter, and then send the stamped deed and PTAX-203 to the Cook County Clerk. If you may qualify for a refund, keep your closing statement and the packet deadline in mind, since requests are due within one year of the sale.

faqs.q: Does Oak Lawn charge a transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The village rate is 5.00 per 1,000 of value, paid by the seller, with exempt transfers needing an exemption letter. Contact the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 for the stamp.

faqs.q: What does the Oak Lawn sewer inspection cost?
faqs.a: The village charges $100, paid by a link emailed after the inspection. It applies to single-family homes and qualifying townhomes and runs between 10am and 2pm.

faqs.q: Are seniors exempt from the transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The village states that seniors selling a primary residence are now exempt, with details in section 3 of its exemption list. A separate refund route exists for sellers 65 or older under ordinance 3-2-7.

faqs.q: How long do I have to ask for a stamp refund?
faqs.a: Refunds must be requested within one year of the date of sale. The village lists reinvestment, senior and immediate family cases, each with its own packet.

faqs.q: Where is an Oak Lawn deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. The sale also needs the PTAX-203 declaration and stamped deed.
